source.title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes

accepted.question_text: For a graph G = (V, E), the Coloring problem asks whether G has a coloring with at most k colors, where a coloring assigns colors to vertices so that adjacent vertices receive different colors. A graph is even-cycle-free if it has no induced cycle of even length, and it is even-anticycle-free if it has no induced subgraph that is the complement of an even cycle. What is the computational complexity of Coloring when the input is restricted to even-cycle-free graphs, and what is the computational complexity of Coloring when the input is restricted to even-anticycle-free graphs?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1 Determine the complexity of Coloring for even-cycle-free graphs and even-anticycle-free graphs.

accepted.question_text: For fixed integers k >= 3 and t, let P_t be the path on t vertices, and say that a graph is P_t-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to P_t. In k-Precoloring Extension, the input is a graph G together with a partial k-coloring of some vertices, and the question is whether that partial coloring can be extended to a proper k-coloring of all of G. In List k-Coloring, every vertex v has a list L(v) contained in {1, ..., k}, and the question is whether G has a proper coloring assigning each vertex a color from its list. For bipartite P_t-free graphs, what is the computational complexity of the unresolved cases: k-Precoloring Extension for t = 7, 8, or 9 with k = 3, 4, 5, or any fixed k >= 6, and for t >= 10 with k = 3; and List k-Coloring for t = 7 with k = 3, 4, 5, or any fixed k >= 6, and for t = 8, t = 9, or t >= 10 with k = 3?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2 Determine the complexity of the problems k-Precoloring Extension and List k-Coloring for the missing cases in Table 1.
Table 1. The complexity of k-Precoloring Extension and List k-Coloring on Pt-free bipartite graphs for fixed k and t.

accepted.question_text: A graph is chordal bipartite if it is bipartite and every induced cycle in it has exactly four vertices. What is the computational complexity of List 3-Coloring on chordal bipartite graphs, where each vertex has a list of allowed colors drawn from {1, 2, 3} and the task is to find a proper coloring respecting the lists? What is the computational complexity of 3-Precoloring Extension on chordal bipartite graphs, where a partial 3-coloring is given and the task is to decide whether it extends to a proper 3-coloring of the whole graph?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3 Determine the complexity of the problems List 3-Coloring and 3-Precoloring Extension for the class of chordal bipartite graphs.
A graph is chordal bipartite if it is bipartite and every induced cycle has exactly four vertices.

accepted.question_text: In Precoloring Extension, the input is a graph G, a positive integer k, and a partial k-coloring of some vertices of G; the question is whether this partial coloring can be extended to a proper k-coloring of all vertices of G. What is the computational complexity of Precoloring Extension when the input graph is restricted to be a grid graph?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4 Determine the complexity of Precoloring Extension for grids.
subgrids (which are induced subgraphs of grids and hence have maximum degree at most 4)

accepted.question_text: The 5-Coloring problem asks whether the vertices of a graph can be colored with colors from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} so that adjacent vertices receive different colors. What is the computational complexity of 5-Coloring for graphs whose maximum vertex degree is at most 6?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5 Determine the complexity of 5-Coloring for graphs of maximum degree 6.

accepted.question_text: For a connected graph, the diameter is the maximum distance between two vertices, where distance is the length of a shortest path. The 3-Coloring problem asks whether a graph has a proper coloring using colors {1, 2, 3}. The List 3-Coloring problem asks whether a graph with lists L(v) contained in {1, 2, 3} for each vertex v has a proper coloring that assigns every vertex a color from its list. What is the computational complexity of 3-Coloring for graphs of diameter 2, and what is the computational complexity of List 3-Coloring for graphs of diameter 2?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6 Determine the complexity of the problems 3-Coloring and List 3-Coloring for graphs of diameter 2.
The diameter of G is the maximum of maxv d(u, v) over all vertices u in G.

accepted.question_text: A graph is AT-free if it has no asteroidal triple: there do not exist three mutually non-adjacent vertices such that each pair is joined by a path avoiding the neighborhood of the third vertex. What is the computational complexity of the Coloring problem on AT-free graphs, where Coloring asks whether a given graph has a proper coloring with at most k colors for an input integer k?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7 Determine the complexity of Coloring for AT-free graphs.
Note that graphs with asteroidal number at most 2 have no asteroidal triple. These graphs are also known as AT-free graphs.

accepted.question_text: An asteroidal set in a graph is an independent set S such that every three vertices of S form an asteroidal triple, and the asteroidal number of a graph is the maximum size of such a set. For every pair of fixed integers k >= 3 and p >= 3, what is the computational complexity on graphs with asteroidal number at most p of the following three problems: k-Coloring, which asks for a proper coloring with colors {1, ..., k}; k-Precoloring Extension, which asks whether a given partial k-coloring extends to a full proper k-coloring; and List k-Coloring, which asks whether a proper coloring exists that respects vertex lists contained in {1, ..., k}?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8 Determine, for every k ≥ 3 and p ≥ 3, the complexity of k-Coloring, k-Precoloring Extension and List k-Coloring on graphs with asteroidal number at most p.
The asteroidal number is the size of a largest asteroidal set in G.

accepted.question_text: A problem is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to a parameter p if instances (I, p) can be solved in time f(p)|I|^O(1) for some computable function f depending only on p. An AT-free graph is a graph with no asteroidal triple. Is the Coloring problem fixed-parameter tractable on AT-free graphs when the parameter is the number k of colors?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9 Is Coloring fixed-parameter tractable for AT-free graphs when parameterized by k?
A problem is called fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) if every instance (I, p) of it can be solved in time f(p)|I|O(1)

accepted.question_text: A comparability graph is an undirected graph whose edges can be oriented so that whenever (u, v) and (v, w) are directed edges, (u, w) is also a directed edge. For a graph class F and integer p, F - pe denotes graphs that can be modified into a graph of F by adding at most p edges, and F + pv denotes graphs that can be modified into a graph of F by deleting at most p vertices. What is the parameterized complexity, with parameter p, of Coloring on comparability - pe graphs and on comparability + pv graphs?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 10 Determine the complexity of Coloring for the classes of comparability−pe graphs and comparability+pv graphs when parameterized by p.
An (undirected) graph is a comparability graph if there exists an assignment of exactly one direction to each of its edges

accepted.question_text: A complete + pv graph is a graph that can be transformed into a complete graph by deleting at most p vertices. In List Coloring, each vertex has a list of admissible colors and the task is to find a proper coloring that respects all lists. In Precoloring Extension, a partial k-coloring is given and the task is to decide whether it extends to a proper k-coloring of the whole graph. What is the parameterized complexity, with parameter p, of List Coloring and of Precoloring Extension on complete + pv graphs?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11 Determine the complexity of List Coloring and Precoloring Extension for complete+pv graphs when parameterized by p.

F + pe, F - pe, F + pv and F - pv, which consist of all graphs that can be modified into a graph of F by deleting at most p edges, adding at most p edges, deleting at most p vertices and adding at most p vertices, respectively.

accepted.question_text: In online graph coloring, vertices are presented one at a time in an externally determined order, and an online algorithm must irrevocably color each vertex using only the already revealed induced subgraph and its colors. For a graph G, chi_OL(G) is the smallest worst-case number of colors used by any online coloring algorithm over all vertex arrival orders. A graph class is online chi_OL-bounded if there is an online coloring algorithm A and a function h such that A uses at most h(chi_OL(G)) colors on every graph G in the class. Are chordal bipartite graphs online chi_OL-bounded?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 12 Is the class of chordal bipartite graphs on-line χOL-bounded?
the graph is presented vertex by vertex according to some externally determined ordering.
In that case G is said to be on-line χOL-bounded.

accepted.question_text: In online graph coloring, vertices are revealed one by one and must be colored irrevocably using only the revealed part of the graph. For each graph G, chi_OL(G) is the minimum, over online coloring algorithms, of the worst-case number of colors used over all vertex orders; a graph class is online chi_OL-bounded if some online coloring algorithm uses at most h(chi_OL(G)) colors for every graph G in the class, for some function h. For every integer k >= 1, is the class of bipartite graphs with no induced path P_k online chi_OL-bounded?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 13 Is the class of Pk-free bipartite graphs on-line χOL-bounded for every k ≥ 1?
We denote the path and cycle on n vertices by Pn and Cn, respectively.

accepted.question_text: In online graph coloring, vertices arrive sequentially and must be colored irrevocably based only on the subgraph seen so far. A graph class is online chi_OL-bounded if some online coloring algorithm has its color usage bounded by a function of chi_OL(G), the optimal online chromatic number of each graph G. Is the class of graphs that are both triangle-free and P6-free, equivalently (C3, P6)-free graphs, online chi_OL-bounded?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 14 Is the class of (C3, P6)-free graphs on-line χOL-bounded?
We denote the path and cycle on n vertices by Pn and Cn, respectively.

accepted.question_text: In online graph coloring, an algorithm receives the vertices of a graph one at a time and irrevocably assigns each new vertex a color using only the revealed subgraph and previous colors. For a graph G, chi_OL(G) is the smallest worst-case number of colors achievable by any online coloring algorithm. Is the class of all graphs online chi_OL-bounded, meaning that there exists an online coloring algorithm whose color use on every graph G is bounded by some function of chi_OL(G)?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 15 Is the class of all graphs on-line χOL-bounded?

Direct shell fetching of zbmath.org failed in the restricted environment with DNS resolution failure, so resolver metadata was used only for identity matching.

Resolved the exact work to an author-hosted PDF whose title and author match the zbMATH/Durham/Springer metadata. The Springer chapter and Durham repository page were treated as resolver/metadata surfaces; extraction used the readable PDF text.
